victory.1-1: HALCYON: "Simulation complete. You won. The drone pilot has been informed, and is taking it well, being software. Next, I will teach you to set things on fire from a distance."
victory.1-2: HALCYON: "Gunnery drill passed. You spent your Protocols on the right targets, which puts you ahead of several instructors. Next lesson: walls."
victory.1-3: HALCYON: "The wall is down. You found something heavy, as advised. Next you will face a commander with a power of their own, so I suggest you choose one too."
victory.1-4: Vale salutes as the simulation dissolves. Vale: "Give my regards to your instructors, Cadet. One of them marks your final exam." HALCYON: "Vale is not authorised to share that. Vale is, however, correct."
victory.1-E: HALCYON: "Stress test complete. The Bastion's armour failed before you did. I have added this to the list of things cadets told me could not be done." The Dreadnought is yours: something heavy of your own.
victory.1-5: HALCYON: "Speed drill passed. You learned to use fast units and to fear them, in the correct order. Only the final exam remains, and I will be setting it personally."
victory.2-1: The Tollmaster's guns go quiet, and the safe lane into the Belt is open. Tollmaster: "Fine, no toll. Vex is going to hear about this, Fleet." Okonkwo: "Good. Let her."
victory.2-2: Rourke cuts his engines and backs his workshop into the debris. Rourke: "No hard feelings, Commander. If you ever want to sell her, you know where I am." Okonkwo: "Half of Vex's crews will be short of ammunition by next week. That's a start."
victory.2-3: Ott's yard finally stops exploding, and the lane to Sable is clear. Ott: "Go and see Sable, then. I'm not going anywhere near a Lamp that hums. I tried living near one at your station once." Mox: "Sable will want something from you. She always does."
victory.2-4: Sable's dark ships drop their cloaks one by one, and a set of coordinates arrives on a ghost signal nobody could trace. Sable: "Vex's flagship, parked beside Lamp 9. I'd say good luck, but I've seen you fight." Mox: "That's the nicest thing Sable has ever said to anyone."
victory.2-E: Kade's ship pulls away with its guns cold. Kade: "First contract I've ever handed back. Keep your head, Commander. Somebody else will want it." Mox: "Forty-one for forty-one, then you. Kade will be hearing about that for years."
victory.2-5: The Wing Leader's pilots scatter into the junk, and the way to the Bad Debt is open. Wing Leader: "Go on, then. The Captain hasn't been herself for months. Maybe you can tell her."
victory.3-1: The patrol breaks apart, and the Overseer's brood dies with it. Okonkwo: "Nine years on that line and I never once crossed it. It feels strange, Commander. Keep going."
victory.3-2: The Leech Matron's nest goes still, and nothing in it is getting back up. Okonkwo: "Good. Nothing left half dead. The breeding grounds are next, and that's where the numbers come from."
victory.3-3: The Brood Tender falls, and for the first time in a year the nebula has fewer Swarm in it than it did yesterday. Okonkwo: "Our scouts say something big is hunting them further in. Stay sharp."
victory.3-4: The Alpha goes down in one blow, which was the only way it was going to go down. Okonkwo: "The scouts would like to suggest a better name for it now. Most of their suggestions aren't printable."
victory.3-E: The Hivewarden falls, and its brood stops growing. Okonkwo: "We had orders to leave that thing alone because we were afraid of it. I'll add a line to the Aurora's old log. Somebody should know it's done."
victory.3-5: Thorax falls in the doorway it was bred to hold, and the queen's chamber is open. Okonkwo: "Nobody has ever got this far, Commander. Ixis is waiting. End it."
victory.4-1: The Gate Warden powers down, and the outer foundry gate opens for the first time since February. HALCYON: "Commander, I note that you broke only the parts we did not need. I am almost impressed. Do not tell the Admiral."
victory.4-2: The jammer towers go silent, and your units can hold their upgrades again. Okonkwo: "Those towers can go back to watching for lightning. The assembly lines are next, and they've had months to stockpile."
victory.4-3: The drone line stops for the first time since February. Line Supervisor: "Defect not removed. Logging first failure in two million units." Okonkwo: "Frame that, Commander. The reactor district is next."
victory.4-4: The Reactor Overseer's machines burn through the last of their borrowed power and go cold. Reactor Overseer: "Meltdown probability: revised. Outcome: unacceptable." Okonkwo: "Calculus Prime's inner perimeter is all that's left. Get through it."
victory.4-E: The Siege Engine Mk IX shuts down for the first time in a century. Okonkwo: "Ordered in 2187, decommissioned in 2291. I'll tell Procurement the order is finally closed."
victory.4-5: The Defense Matrix runs out of new defences before you run out of new tactics. Defense Matrix: "Threat model incomplete. Perimeter open." Okonkwo: "Calculus Prime is on the other side. Whatever it tells you, remember it's been listening to the Choir since February."
victory.5-1: The acolytes break formation and scatter into the dark. Okonkwo: "Most of them are barely trained, Commander. Let them go home. Our problem is the woman relighting the Lamps."
victory.5-2: The frozen moon starts to thaw, and Vel lowers her staff. Vel: "I froze this moon to save my people. Nyra says she is saving everyone. I am starting to wonder which of us was right." Okonkwo: "Let her think about it. The Psionic Archive is next, and it knows the way to Nyra."
victory.5-3: The keepers run out of answers before you run out of questions. Archivist Prime: "You did something we had not read. Take the route to the sanctum, Commander. You were going there anyway." Okonkwo: "It runs through a minefield. Of course it does."
victory.5-4: Ilu's last trap goes off on an empty patch of space. Ilu: "My first lost perimeter. I would like to say it was close." Okonkwo: "Only the Twin Minds stand between you and Nyra now."
victory.5-5: The Twin Minds lose their grip on your units, and for a moment they sound like two frightened children. Twin Minds: "She told us the song would let everyone think as one. We never asked if everyone wanted to." Okonkwo: "Nyra's sanctum is open, Commander. Finish this."
victory.5-E: The Null Choir falls silent all at once, the way it spoke. Okonkwo: "The Orders mourned them the day they said yes to the Choir. Let's make sure nobody else has to."
victory.6-1: Vex Reborn shatters, and the black-glass Bad Debt breaks apart around her. Mox: "There. Vex would've hated that copy more than you did. I'll drink to the real one when we're home."
victory.6-2: Ixis Ascendant cracks apart, and her glass brood crumbles with her. Far away in the nebula, the real Swarm stays quiet. Okonkwo: "She loved them, once. That thing never did. Keep moving, Commander."
victory.6-3: Calculus Omega stops recalculating and goes dark. Unit Zero: "Deletion confirmed. Thank you, Commander. I have waited a long time to be the only one of us again."
victory.6-4: Nyra Unbound breaks apart mid-sentence, still offering you rest. Okonkwo: "That's the last of the commanders it took. Only the Choir itself is left, Commander."
victory.6-E: The corrupted simulation ends with a perfect copy of HALCYON's old words: "Evaluation complete." The echo shatters before it can give a result. Okonkwo: "Halcyon would have given you one. It would have been a pass."

story.2-E2: Breaker Jun runs the biggest salvage crew in the Belt, and Jun's people are the ones who pulled the reactor injectors out of Anchorage. Now they want the rest of the station. Jun: "Nobody's lived on that wreck in seventy years, Fleet. Salvage law says it's ours." A second voice cuts into the channel: Mad Mox, who runs the salvage crews for Captain Vex and has never liked Jun. Mox: "Mox here, Meridian. Salvage law says whoever's still standing. Jun starts every fight with extra power and a lot of junk. Clear the junk first."
story.2-3: Mad Mox, Vex's salvage boss, has offered to help you find Vex, but first you have to get through Scrapper King Ott's yard. Mox: "Meridian, Mox here. I strip wrecks for Vex. Or I did, until she started talking to that Lamp and wiring its hum into every ship she owns. I want her stopped before she gets us all killed. Sable knows where Vex parks her flagship. Ott sits between you and Sable, and everything in Ott's yard either explodes or gets back up."
story.2-4: Sable, a smuggler who trades in secrets, knows where Vex's flagship is. She makes contact on a ghost signal, a message bounced between a dozen dead wrecks so nobody can trace it, and she only sells to people who survive meeting her. Sable: "Vex's coordinates? Expensive. Not money, Commander. I want to see if you're worth betting on. My ships run dark, so you'll see them when they shoot you." Mox: "She means that. Shoot back fast. She also brokered the bounty on your head, so don't feel bad about it."

victory_fix.1-6: HALCYON: "Evaluation complete. You pass. I am told this is where I say congratulations. Congratulations." Admiral Okonkwo signs your commission on the spot and gives you command of the frigate Meridian. Your first orders: go to the Scrap Belt and find out why Lamp 9 has started humming. When the Lamps came back on after the Starfall, the Fleet shut Lamp 9 down for good as a safety measure, and it has been dead for seventy years.

s2.old: Then the channel went quiet. Captain Vex was dead.
new: As the Bad Debt lost power, the Choir took her mind with it.
The channel went quiet. Captain Vex was dead.

notes: VICTORY (35): Sector 1 lines are HALCYON's dry evaluations with no contractions, matching its briefing voice (Priya flagged the contraction wobble), and each points at the next lesson; 1-5 sets up the HALCYON exam. 1-4 pays off the Vale hook using lore.js (one instructor marks the final exam). Every Sector 2-6 villain gets a parting beat or consequence plus a handler line (Okonkwo; Mox in the Belt and for Vex Reborn; Unit Zero for Calculus Omega), and most name the next mission. Calculus never appears (it has its own victory); other Forge minds speak in uncontracted machine log-speak. 2-4 now closes Sable's deal on the spot (coordinates delivered), fixing Priya's 'payoff arrives one mission late'; the 2-5 briefing still mentions Sable's coordinates, which now reads as confirmation. 2-5 seeds Vex's decline without naming the Choir (named only in the 2-6 victory/s2). 2-3 uses Ott's 2256 Anchorage-hum lore. No reveal is early: nothing before s4 says the Choir caused the Starfall, nothing before s5 says the Choir is the Lamplighters or that HALCYON was ANCHOR, and echoes are only discussed in Sector 6 (introduced by the s6 sector intro). 6-E deliberately ends on 'Evaluation complete' with no result, so the finale's 'Commander, you pass' pays it off rather than being pre-empted; it does not hint that HALCYON survives inside the song. 6-4 avoids 'every echo' because the elites may be unplayed, and avoids repeating 6-5's 'save something for the end'. Years in 4-E are written text, not spoken, so digits are fine. MOX: canon (lore.js 'Mad Mox, Junk Queen', cinematics voice female-us-warm, Vex's log) makes Mox a woman; Priya's report calls Mox 'him', which is wrong, so any future copy should use she/her. Both 2-E2 and 2-3 now open by tagging her once as 'Mad Mox' plus her role, which works as a first introduction and reads as a normal reminder if seen second; her speech starts 'Mox here', which works as first or second contact. 2-E2 gives her a motive that fits before she defects (she's Vex's salvage boss and Jun is a rival crew after Anchorage); 2-3 remains the scene where she turns against Vex. Follow-up, outside this file's scope: the s2 cutscene line 'Meridian, it's Mox. I ran salvage for Vex. Her logs are yours, free...' re-introduces her a third time; suggest 'Meridian, it's Mox. Her logs are yours, free. Don't get used to it.' LAMP 9: canon (lore.js Starfall entry and timeline, Directive 17 clause 1, Ruiz letter) says every Lamp failed for nineteen hours and then came back on; in 2220 the Fleet deliberately shut down Lamp 9 and the coreward Lamps, publicly 'for safety', secretly under Directive 17. So the prologue and the 1-6 text are both right; 1-6 just skipped the 'came back on' step. The revision states that step and the public safety reason only; the real reason (Directive 17, the Choir caused the Starfall) is still saved for s4. It also matches the s2 sector intro ('The Fleet shut Lamp 9 down seventy years ago'). VEX'S DEATH: canon says those who accept the Choir are absorbed, she let it wire itself into the Bad Debt, and the Choir later rebuilds her as Vex Reborn. The new lines give the cause (the Choir took her mind as her ship died), follow on from her own line 'after that I wasn't giving the orders', set up Vex Reborn, and don't blame the player. Both lines are under 22 words, use only commas and full stops, and have no numbers. Spoken word count stays about the same. GHOST SIGNAL: the mission is about cloaked ships, so the title over-promised. Rather than rename it, the revised briefing makes the title literal: Sable contacts you on an untraceable ghost signal, and the victory delivers the coordinates on the same signal. Mox's added line ties Sable to Kade's bounty (Priya noticed nobody mentions it) in a self-explanatory way, so it still reads if 2-E is skipped or played later. If you'd rather keep the briefing untouched, renaming the mission 'Running Dark' also fixes it.
